concept: One system diagram on the plain light field, held for the whole lesson: the browser window at left, the server at right, a short path of network nodes between them with a watcher on one node. The same login packet makes the trip again and again while the system changes state on the spoken word: readable and copied, then wrapped in TLS, the certificate checked row by row, two signals crossing to become one identical key at each end, the packet scrambled to noise and back, the padlock closing beside the address. A step bar along the bottom lights the three moves. The check moves to a quiz on the same field; the close replays the opening trip, now as noise.

stations.note: Browser window left (about x 110 to 630, y 150 to 700), server right (about x 1430 to 1810, y 170 to 700), the network path at about y 430 between them with four nodes, the watcher on the second node (about x 1000), the watcher panel space above the path (about y 150 to 330), the certificate check panel space centre (about x 660 to 1300, y 150 to 640) for b05 to b07, the step bar along the bottom (about y 770 to 880). Nothing readable below y 930 (captions).
quiz.question then quiz.answer on the plain field, b15 and b16.

story.metaphor: None: the literal system, browser to server, shown as a clean diagram that changes state.
story.setting: A plain light field: one browser, one server, the shared network between them.
story.arc: A login crosses shared wifi readable and is copied; three moves make it private: the certificate proves who, a key exchange agrees a key the watcher cannot work out, the key scrambles the login to noise; the padlock means that private trip, not a verdict on the site; checked on a quiz; the opening trip replayed as noise.

devices.what: The held system: browser window (address bar, padlock slot, key slot), network path of four nodes, server box (name label, key slot, data store). Never redrawn; it changes state.
Three step tiles along the bottom (1 Prove who, 2 Agree a key, 3 Scramble): appear in b03, each lights as its move starts, all three in b17.
The one login packet that travels the path: plain readable, wrapped in TLS, scrambled to noise, tampered and rejected, noise again at the close.
What the watcher on the path holds: the readable password, then two recorded signals and a question mark, then noise. A callback each time.
The certificate card with three check rows (Issuer, Name, Date) that tick in turn; one fails into the warning.
The one join material: hard cuts only at the opening, into the check (b15) and back to the held system for the close (b17); every other join continues the held stage.

parts.what: A clean flat browser window card (surface, r 20, offset shadow, ink title strip with three small muted dots). Address bar with the address text as a parameter (default login.example.com; a scheme prefix that can read http:// or https://), a padlock slot just left of the address, a content area that shows a small login form (two fields: user and password, a Log in button in muted, not blue). A key slot at the window's lower right edge (shared with the key part). Can show a warning panel over its content area (surface card, a neg cross mark, ink text Warning, a muted line Name does not match) that stops the packet. Exports anchors: address, padlock, key_slot, packet_out (the right edge where the path starts), check_panel origin.

The server: a flat rack of three stacked units in surface with surface2 edges and small muted status dots (no blue), its name label login.example.com on a white pill hanging below it, a key slot at its left edge, and a small data store drum below or behind it (accent3 slate) that can be outlined dashed as not covered. Exports anchors: packet_in (left edge), key_slot, data_store, cert_out.

The path between browser and server: a 3 px line in line token with four round nodes (surface2 discs, 2 px line edge); the first node labelled Shared wifi (label 28 px muted). A method to move a token along it from either end (positions 0 to 1). A trip_band state: the line between the two ends thickens to a solid band (accent when named, ink otherwise) for the private trip. Exports node anchors node1 to node4 and a point at any position.

The passive watcher: an ink disc on node 2 with a white Lucide eye icon (eye can be closed, open, or pulse once), and its panel above the node (surface card, r 20, title Watcher in muted) that shows one of: copied (a copy of the packet with user and password readable in mono ink), signals (the two recorded signal chips, slate and amber, and a dashed key slot holding a large ink question mark), noise (a block of scrambled mono glyphs from a fixed seeded string, muted). Never a person, never a face.

The login packet: a small card token (about 200 x 120) that travels the path. States: plain (title Login, two mono lines user: alex and password: harbour, readable), wrapped (the same card inside a 4 px accent outline with a TLS tab), noise (the card's text replaced by a seeded block of scrambled mono glyphs, a morph from plain to noise and back as it passes through a key), altered (one glyph block in the noise swaps to a visibly different block), rejected (a neg cross mark on it, it dims and stops). Accent only when the narration names it.

A certificate card (surface, r 20, a small ribbon seal in accent3) with the site name login.example.com as its title and three rows: Issuer (Trusted authority), Name (login.example.com), Date (a short validity bar with a today marker inside its range: no digits). Each row has a mark slot at its right: empty, tick (kit.mark yes), cross (kit.mark no). Row highlight state puts the row label in accent while it is spoken. A small form to travel from the server to the browser, and a large form (about 620 x 420) in the check panel space. A thin line can join the Name row to the browser's address.

The key exchange parts: an own mark at each end that never leaves (a small square chip: slate at the browser, amber at the server), a travelling signal chip in the same two colours (the browser's slate signal goes right, the server's amber signal goes left), an empty dashed key slot at each end, and the key: one key shape with a notched bit pattern, IDENTICAL at both ends, which forms where a received signal meets that side's own mark. Key states: empty, forming, named (accent fill), held (ink fill). The key itself is never drawn on the path.

A small flat padlock beside the address in the browser bar (about 44 px in the bar; a larger 96 px form for the close): open (shackle up, muted) and closed (shackle down, accent when named, ink when held), with a close motion.

Three step tiles in one row along the bottom (about 1200 wide, centre x 960, y 780 to 870): 1 Prove who, 2 Agree a key, 3 Scramble, each a white card with a numbered disc. States per tile: hidden, shown (neutral), named (accent fill, white text, while spoken), done (ink disc with a pos tick, card neutral). All three can show done together.

kit.notes: No people, no presenter, no faces anywhere. Corporate-clean tokens only (guide s2): one blue element or one blue family per settled frame, the one the narration names; everything else ink, muted, line, surface, surface2, accent3 slate. The two key-exchange colours are slate (accent3) and amber (accent2); the key turns blue only when named. pos and neg only as kit.mark ticks and crosses and tags under 300 x 60. Labels 28 px or larger, body weight 500, names 700; Lucide icons only; radii by role (20 cards, 14 bezels, 10 tags, 6 inner fields). Every word on screen is the lesson's: login.example.com and the look-alike login-example.co are fictional illustration addresses; user: alex and password: harbour are illustration values. Noise glyphs come from a fixed seeded string (Loom.rng), never Math.random.

scenes.subject: A key exchange: the key never travels

design.treatment: Each end shows its own mark that stays home (slate at the browser, amber at the server). A slate signal leaves the browser and an amber signal leaves the server; they cross at the watcher's node and arrive at the far ends. At each end the received signal meets that side's own mark and the slot fills with the same notched key, blue as it lands. The key is never drawn on the path.
design.why_motion: the exchange is the idea: what crosses is not the key, and the key forms only at the ends
